Rashi on Gittin 70a:10:1.hebrew: אכול שליש - מלא מעיך שליש, ושתה שליש, והנח שליש בטנך ריקם:
Rashi on Gittin 70a:10:1.english: Eat a third - Fill your stomach a third, and drink a third, and leave a third of your stomach empty:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:10:2.hebrew: ולכשתכעוס - וימלא בטנך כעס, תעמוד על מילואך; אבל אם תמלא מעיך אכילה ושתיה, לכשתכעוס תבקע:
Rashi on Gittin 70a:10:2.english: And when you become angry - and your stomach fills with anger, you will be at your full capacity; but if you fill your innards with food and drink, when you become angry you will burst:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:11:1.english: In dipping - To dip [one's food] in vinegar, or bread in wine:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:11:2.english: That you enjoy - that is pleasing to you:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:11:3.english: Withdraw your hand from it - so that you do not fill your belly.

Rashi on Gittin 70a:12:3.english: Fragrant - that it has a very good aroma:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:13:1.english: During the mornings - In the mornings:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:14:1.english: He will have - If she conceived from that intercourse:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:14:2.hebrew: בעלי ראתן - חלשים הרבה, מחמת שיש להן שרץ במוח, כדאמרינן בכתובות (דף עז:):
Rashi on Gittin 70a:14:2.english: [Children] afflicted with ra'atan - [They are] very weak, because they have a creeping creature in their brain, as we say in Ketubot (77b):

Rashi on Gittin 70a:14:3.english: [If] he did not taste anything - between bloodletting and intercourse:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:17:1.english: The remedy [for] dalarya - The remedy for healing dalarya is called dardara:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:17:2.hebrew: מוריקא דחוחי - קרו"ג הגדל בגדר של היזמי, שקורין שבי"ל:
Rashi on Gittin 70a:17:2.english: Saffron of thorns - [This is] crocus [Old French: crog] that grows in a hedge of thorns, which they call sevil:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:18:1.english: In [the] way of the world - [meaning] that he does not have the strength to engage in marital relations:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:18:2.english: Kefiza - a vessel that holds three-quarters [of a log]:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:18:3.english: And let us grind them - he should pound them finely:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:18:4.english: To my youth - [With regard] to sexual intercourse:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:19:1.hebrew: פחד - דאגה שדואג על דבר העתיד, כגון טירוד מזונות או פחד אויב, וקורין סיינש"א:
Rashi on Gittin 70a:19:1.english: Fear - Worry that one has about a future matter, such as preoccupation with sustenance or fear of an enemy, and [in Old French] they call [it] "seinsa" [anxiety]:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:1:1.english: Grapes of ta'ala - grapes of a vine that is trellised on a palm tree:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:21:1.hebrew: אכל ועמד - מיד, קודם ששהה מעט:
Rashi on Gittin 70a:21:1.english: Ate and stood - [meaning he stood up] immediately, before waiting a little:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:22:1.english: One who performs them - all of them at once:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:24:1.hebrew: ומיעוטן יפה - כשיש לאדם מעט מהם, יפה לגופו לרפואה, וטוב שיהא לו קצת משלא יהא לו כלום:
Rashi on Gittin 70a:24:1.english: And a small amount of them is beneficial - When a person has a little of them, [it is] beneficial for his body for healing, and [it is] better that he have a little than that he have nothing at all:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:24:2.english: But a large amount of them is harmful - when one has much [of them]:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:24:4.english: And the way of the world - [Sexual] intercourse:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:24:5.hebrew: עושר - מיעוטו יפה ורובו קשה, שמבטלו מת"ת ומגביה לבבו:
Rashi on Gittin 70a:24:5.english: Wealth - A small amount of it is beneficial, and a large amount of it is harmful, for it causes him to neglect Torah study and makes him haughty:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:24:6.english: Hot water - to bathe [in] and to drink:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:25:3.english: Not in its time - Further on [the Gemara] explains:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:25:4.english: And bloodletting below - it diminishes [the semen] twice as much as all of them:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:2:1.english: For chazazita - [This is] yallefet [a type of skin rash or lichen]:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:2:3.english: On a new hoe - On the iron [blade] of a new hoe [Old French: fosoir]:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:2:4.english: And let him rub [it] - He should smear [it]:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:3:1.english: With Persian spears [alunkei] - With lances of the Persians, which they temper in deadly poison:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:3:2.english: [That] he may instruct his household - [i.e., make] a will regarding his property:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:6:1.hebrew: מכל דבר - שהוא טוב לו ומתוק לחיכו, ואוכל ממנו כל תאוותו, מביאו לידי חולי ששמו אחילו:
Rashi on Gittin 70a:6:1.english: With anything - [Anything] that is good for him and sweet to his palate, and he eats of it [according to] all his desire, brings him to an illness whose name is achilu:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:6:2.english: Since the Master said - that dates are so beneficial to the body:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:6:6.hebrew: ולא מפנקן - אינן מתענגות את הלב להיות איסטניס, ואע"פ שהן מתוקות:
Rashi on Gittin 70a:6:6.english: And do not spoil [it] - They do not pamper the heart so as to make [one] delicate, even though they are sweet:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:8:1.hebrew: כל שקייני - כל משקין שאדם שותה לרפואה, יש להן מנין ימים לשתותם: יש מהן ג', יש מהן ז', יש מהן י"ב:
Rashi on Gittin 70a:8:1.english: All shakyanei - All drinks that a person drinks for healing have a [set] number of days to drink them: some of them [for] three [days], some of them [for] seven [days], [and] some of them [for] twelve [days]:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:9:1.hebrew: בונא דשתיתא דטלפחי - מלא אגרוף מן שתיתא, שם מאכל העשוי מקמח עדשים ומלח:
Rashi on Gittin 70a:9:1.english: Buna of shetita of lentils - A fistful of shetita, [which is] the name of a food made from lentil flour and salt:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:9:2.english: And let him wrap his body in sheets - in order that his body warms up and sweats:

Rashi on Gittin 70a:9:3.hebrew: וליכא דנוקמיה - ולא יהיה אדם שיקיצנו, לפי שהזיעה יפה לו:
Rashi on Gittin 70a:9:3.english: And let there be no [one] who will awaken him - And there should not be any person who wakes him up, because sweating is beneficial for him:

Tosafot on Gittin 70a:19:1.hebrew: דרך ועון - דאגת העון, א"נ עונש העון:
Tosafot on Gittin 70a:19:1.english: Road and sin - [This refers to] worry over the sin, or alternatively, the punishment for the sin:

Tosafot on Gittin 70a:21:1.hebrew: חמשה קרובין למיתה אכל ועמד כו' - משמע אפילו עושה אחד מהן בלבד, מדלא קאמרינן עלה דבעינן כסדרן:
Tosafot on Gittin 70a:21:1.english: Five [things] are closer to death; he ate and stood [up], etc. - [This] implies [that this is so] even if one does only one of them, since [the Gemara] does not say regarding it that we require [them] in their order:

Tosafot on Gittin 70a:2:1.hebrew: רב שימי בר אשי עבד ליה לההוא עובד כוכבים כו' - הקשה ה"ר אלחנן: אמאי לא אסור לרפאות העובד כוכבים, כדאמרינן בפ' אין מעמידין (ע"ז דף כו.) גבי מילדת ומניקה, אפילו בשכר, לפי שמגדלו לעבודת כוכבים? ואור"י, דשמא כדי להתחכם ברפואה שרי, כדי שידע לרפאות ישראל ע"י כן; א"נ, העובד כוכבים היה יודע שהיה בקי ברפואה זאת, ושרי משום איבה; או שמא לא שייך כאן "מגדל בן לעבודת כוכבים" כמו במילדת ומניקה:
Tosafot on Gittin 70a:2:1.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi did [it] for a certain idolater, etc. - Rabbi Elḥanan raised a difficulty: Why is it not forbidden to heal the idolater, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Ein Ma'amidin (Avodah Zarah 26a) regarding a midwife and a wet nurse, [that it is forbidden] even for a fee, because she raises him for idolatry? And Rabbeinu Yitzḥak says that perhaps [it is] permitted in order to become skilled in medicine, so that he will know [how] to heal a Jew through this. Alternatively, the idolater knew that he was expert in this remedy, and it is permitted because of [fear of] enmity. Or perhaps "raising a child for idolatry" does not apply here as [it does] with a midwife and a wet nurse:
